reader.requirement: At 1985 the RECORD KEY clause's data-name-1 may be written with qualifiers (IN/OF data-names and/or the file-name), must resolve uniquely, and admits no subscript nor the SOURCE phrase.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.SubscriptedClauseOperands (2002 only) admits a subscripted key
ConstructRegistry RecordKeySource2002: SOURCE phrase refused at 1985

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: the SOURCE phrase is refused at 1985 (k7) and accepted at 2023; qualification is the same code
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf21_09 covers OF record-name qualification against a same-named WORKING-STORAGE item; not covered: file-name qualifier, multi-level qualification, the ambiguous unqualified refusal

probes.printed: RECORD KEY IS K OF REC-F IN IX-F and K OF IX-G: PRI AAA dat1, G 009 gdat FS 0000
probes.expected: qualified keys resolve to the file's own record items; random READ by primary key returns record 001

probes.printed: error COBOL1639 RECORD KEY 'K' does not uniquely identify a data item (3 declarations)
probes.expected: refused: unqualified non-unique name, even though one candidate is in the file's record

probes.printed: --std 85: error COBOL0900 SOURCE phrase requires COBOL-2002; --std 2023: compiles and runs

reader.notes: Same resolver as the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause (InRecords in ResolveFiles). A name ambiguous across files is refused rather than disambiguated by SR2's in-file constraint, which matches §1985:IV.4.3.8.1's uniqueness requirement.

refuter.evidence: q1.cob --std 85 (runs/q1-001): RECORD KEY IS K OF IX-F (file-name qualifier, K also present in IX-G's record), RECORD KEY IS KK OF REC-G (a group key qualified by its record), RECORD KEY IS REC-H OF IX-H (the 01 record itself as the key, qualified by its file-name): WRITE/READ by each returned the record (H HHHHH 00, G 009 gdat 00). The reader's k2 covers the ambiguous unqualified refusal and k7 the SOURCE phrase. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.2.7.3 SR1  (2.7.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1'.
